# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Feb 2, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing contract security by blocking beta tags in production upgrades, improving transaction manager efficiency for blob transactions, and updating Rust subtrees. Several new pull requests were opened, addressing supernode functionality, interop message validation, and developer tooling.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Contract Security and Upgrade Process
A new feature was added to prevent contracts with beta tags from being used in production upgrades, ensuring greater stability and security for the Optimism ecosystem. This enhancement directly contributes to protocol security and decentralization. ([#19035](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19035))

### Transaction Manager Improvements
The transaction manager was updated to utilize blob tip caps when increasing fees for blob transactions, improving the efficiency and accuracy of fee management for these specific transaction types. This change includes new test coverage to ensure proper functionality. ([#19028](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19028))

### Rust Subtree Updates and Build Process Refinements
All Rust subtrees, including `op-alloy` and `op-reth`, were updated to their latest versions. Additionally, workarounds were implemented for older `buildx` versions and `just` versioning in legacy Kona prestate builds, streamlining the development and build processes. ([#19025](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19025), [#19031](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19031), [#19046](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19046))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- [#19053](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19053) supernode: Handle genesis L2 block in L1AtSafeHead lookup
- [#19052](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19052) fix: only allow enabling permissioned game types in opcm v2
- [#19051](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19051) op-supernode: Interop Message Validation
- [#19050](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19050) feat(op-reth): pull latest superchain config on startup
- [#19049](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19049) feat(op-deployer): e2e parallel test protection
- [#19048](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19048) op-devstack: add sysgo integration for op-interop-filter
- [#19045](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19045) feat(op-node): add generic upgrade gas mechanism
- [#19044](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19044) feat(op-reth-hist-proofs): Import op-reth historical proofs code from op-rs fork
- [#19043](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19043) feat(op-reth-hist-proofs): Move op-reth binary into subdir
- [#19042](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19042) add skip-heavy-fuzz label support for ci
- [#19041](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19041) test(contracts): enhance LegacyMintableERC20 test coverage

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were opened today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Supernode Safe Label Adjusting
Discussion on [#18976](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18976) continues regarding the `op-supernode`'s handling of safe labels. The latest comments from `geoknee` propose a model where the Consensus Layer (CL) maintains a full set of pointers (Unsafe, Safe, Finalized) and remains the sole controller of the Execution Layer (EL) engine, except for interop resets. This approach aims to avoid conflicts from multiple stateful controllers and aligns with the existing `op-node` engine controller's interop-aware data structures. `axelKingsley` praised the detailed diagram and terminology, noting that the proposed design seems viable as long as the CL correctly applies local safe payloads. A key concern is how to differentiate between "Local Safe" and "Super Node Safe" in RPC responses from virtual nodes. `geoknee` also outlined options for the interop activity to read data from the CL and EL without causing deadlocks, suggesting either a new "local safe" label in EL or having the supernode communicate with the CL to determine which blocks to retrieve from the EL.

### Flashblocks Support within Geth
The discussion on [#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/756) highlights the internal addition of Flashblocks support in `op-geth` for processing events and tracing. `maoueh` provided a link to their `op-geth` version, which includes Firehose Live Tracer and Flashblock(s) support. `sunjiahui` expressed enthusiasm for merging this functionality into `op-geth`, citing the high disk space consumption and complexity of running archive versions of Reth.

### BlockNotFoundError in Withdrawal Proof
Issue [#1956](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/1956) addresses a `BlockNotFoundError` encountered during the withdrawal proof step in the ETH bridge tutorial. `opfocus` noted that while the Optimism SDK includes output root validation, Viem's withdrawal guide and actions do not appear to perform equivalent validation. This lack of validation can lead to issues when a withdrawal is initiated, and `waitToProve` is executed before the state root is published to L1. `opfocus` provided a detailed temporary workaround involving manually retrieving and overriding output root data from Etherscan to proceed with the `buildProveWithdrawal` action.
